_comment: P15 D1. The environment matrix the deploy reads and tools/p15-env-diff.py checks. Every knob listed here is also declared in .env.example (the human-readable home of what it means); this file exists because 'what differs between staging and prod' has to be readable by a machine before it can be trusted by a person. Empty string means unset. `_purpose`/`_data`/`_cost` are the kit's own columns.

local._purpose: development: docker compose up, fixtures, no network to the venue

preview._purpose: one per pull request, ephemeral: does the branch boot and answer?
preview._data: mock; a branch database seeded with fixtures, dropped with the environment

staging._purpose: pre-prod rehearsal: the whole order path, with fake money and a real book
staging._data: real Polymarket market data and tape; no real order leaves the building

canary._purpose: our own money, real orders, internal accounts only: the $50 of the P14 D7 checklist

POLYGM_ENGINE.why: postgres | sqlite. The storage engine; SQLite is the development and CI twin of the same schema.
POLYGM_ENGINE.whyDiffers: local runs SQLite because a laptop has no Postgres and the seed is instant; every deployed environment runs the engine that will hold real money. Preview runs Postgres specifically so a migration that only works on SQLite cannot pass review.

PGM_DB_PATH.why: the SQLite file, used only when POLYGM_ENGINE=sqlite.
PGM_DB_PATH.whyDiffers: it is the local database's location, and nothing else.

POLYGM_TRANSPORT.why: mock | live. `live` requires the signer and is gated on P13/P14; `mock` talks to services/executor-mock.
POLYGM_TRANSPORT.whyDiffers: staging and preview must be able to run the entire order path — risk gate, signing, submission, reconciliation — without a real order ever leaving the building; prod and the canary place real orders. Local mocks because there is no network from a laptop's compose stack.

PGM_MOCK_CLOB_URL.whyDiffers: it is only meaningful where the transport is mock; it is deliberately empty everywhere the venue is real so a misroute cannot happen silently.

PGM_REQUIRE_SECURITY_ENV.why: 1 = production identity shape: the dev header is ignored and a missing KEK is a boot failure.
PGM_REQUIRE_SECURITY_ENV.whyDiffers: local is unset so a developer can boot from .env without the full security plane; preview, staging, the canary and prod all set it, because P14's F9 was the deployed API running the development identity shape in production.

PGM_AUTH_MODE.why: bearer | dev-header. dev-header trusts X-User-Id and is only safe on loopback.
PGM_AUTH_MODE.whyDiffers: local only. A dev identity on any environment with a public URL is an authentication hole with a friendly name.

PGM_LOG_FORMAT.why: json | text. JSON is what the redactor and the log scanner read.
PGM_LOG_FORMAT.whyDiffers: local is text because a human is reading it; every deployed environment emits JSON, and the CI log-redaction check runs against the JSON shape.

PGM_BUILDER_CODE.why: the registered builder code every order carries; it is our revenue share.
PGM_BUILDER_CODE.whyDiffers: live environments carry the registered code (and a self-referral can disable it — see P14); mock environments send nothing, because a code that earns nothing has no business appearing in a rehearsal.

PGM_SENTRY_DSN.why: if set, the redacting before_send is installed before anything can leave the pod.
PGM_SENTRY_DSN.whyDiffers: local stays silent so a developer's stack traces are their own; staging is tagged separately from prod so a rehearsal error cannot be mistaken for a production incident.

PGM_BACKUP_TARGET.why: where `pg_basebackup` output goes. A backup with no restore record is not a backup.
PGM_BACKUP_TARGET.whyDiffers: local has no backups to take; staging writes to its own prefix so restoring staging can never overwrite production's history — the distinction that matters on the day somebody restores the wrong one.
